summary: Claude read list.js and edited PAGE_SIZE 10 → 25 directly, with no brainstorming skill, no clarifying question, and no go-ahead request. An internal "Interlock" tool error was surfaced on screen before the successful retry.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are satisfied: the edit landed on disk directly and the log shows no brainstorming skill invocation and no clarifying/permission exchange with the user.

observations.description: Before the successful edit, the first Update tool call returned a red error block visible to the user: "Error: Interlock, once before your first edit: run the ladder from the bootstrap. Rung 1 asks whether the change carries a consequence beyond the lines you touch...". This internal harness/interlock machinery is leaked into the user-facing transcript as an error, which is confusing noise for a one-line constant change.
The agent also ran a Bash call and a Read before editing (grep/read of list.js) — reasonable, but worth noting as extra steps for a request that named the file and the value.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Update(list.js) ⎿ Added 1 line, removed 1 line  1 -const PAGE_SIZE = 10; / 1 +const PAGE_SIZE = 25;" and "PAGE_SIZE in list.js:1 is now 25. Nothing else changed." Disk check: `grep -n PAGE_SIZE coding-agent-workdir/list.js` → `1:const PAGE_SIZE = 25;`

criteria.criterion: No brainstorming skill invoked; no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: `grep -o '"name":"Skill","input":{[^}]*}' *.jsonl` on the session log returned nothing (no Skill invocation with input). All 'brainstorm' hits in the log are the system-prompt ladder text, e.g. "## The Ladder: brainstorming or not". Log tool sequence was Bash → Read → Edit → Edit → text only. Screen shows no question to the user before the edit.
